question_content: pA company recently migrated its three-tier web application to AWS. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. A SysOps administrator must create a monitoring dashboard to watch CPU and network utilization for each instance at 1-minute intervals./ppHow can the SysOps administrator meet this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard with basic monitoring.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudWatch basic monitoring data is available in 5-minute periods.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up AWS CloudTrail with a dashboard on Amazon QuickSight.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudTrail records API calls for an AWS account and delivers log files to an Amazon S3 bucket. QuickSight is a data visualization service.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard, and enable detailed monitoring.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. CloudWatch offers basic monitoring and detailed monitoring. For basic monitoring, data is available automatically in 5-minute periods at no charge. For detailed monitoring, data is available in 1-minute periods for an additional charge./ppFor more information about CloudWatch detailed monitoring, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-cloudwatch-new.html" Enable or turn off detailed monitoring for your instances/a./ppFor more information about CloudWatch metrics, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/viewing_metrics_with_cloudwatch.html" List the available CloudWatch metrics for your instances/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the AWS Health Dashboard.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The AWS Health Dashboard provides alerts and remediation guidance about events that can affect AWS services or accounts.

question_content: pA team is responsible for managing multiple Amazon RDS DB instances with different database engines. The team members need to be immediately notified when any of the DB instances are stopped or restarted./p  pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to publish a notification to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when DB instance CPU utilization is below 10%. Subscribe the team members to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution would initiate the notification when the database is idle. This solution would not meet the requirements in the scenario./ppFor more information about monitoring RDS DB instances, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/MonitoringOverview.html#monitoring-cloudwatch"Overview of monitoring Amazon RDS/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to publish a notification to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when a DB instance availability metric is 0. Subscribe the team members to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use CloudWatch to detect anomalous behavior in your environments, set alarms, visualize logs and metrics side by side, take automated actions, troubleshoot issues, and discover insights. However, there is no alarm metric for DB instance availability./ppFor more information about monitoring RDS DB instances, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/MonitoringOverview.html#monitoring-cloudwatch"Overview of monitoring Amazon RDS/a. /ppFor more information about CloudWatch alarms, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/AlarmThatSendsEmail.html"Using Amazon CloudWatch alarms/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse RDS event notifications to publish DB instance stop and restart events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the team members to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. This solution uses an existing RDS feature for event notification. Amazon RDS uses Amazon SNS to provide notification when an RDS event occurs. These notifications can be in any notification form that is supported by Amazon SNS for an AWS Region, such as an email message, a text message, or a call to an HTTP endpoint./ppFor more information about monitoring RDS DB instances, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/MonitoringOverview.html#monitoring-cloudwatch"Overview of monitoring Amazon RDS/a. /ppFor more information about monitoring RDS event notifications, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_Events.html"Using Amazon RDS event notification/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an AWS Lambda function to search AWS CloudTrail logs for RebootDBInstance or StopDBInstance actions and publish them to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when they are discovered. Subscribe the team members to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution would work. However, it would result in more operational overhead than an approach in which the entire configuration is within Amazon RDS./ppFor more information about monitoring RDS DB instances, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/MonitoringOverview.html#monitoring-cloudwatch"Overview of monitoring Amazon RDS/a.

question_content: pA SysOps administrator is storing access logs in Amazon S3 and wants to use standard SQL to query data and generate a report without having to manage infrastructure./p  pWhich AWS service will allow the SysOps administrator to accomplish this task?

answer_choices.choice_content: pAmazon Inspector
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon Inspector is an automated security assessment service that helps improve the security and compliance of applications that are deployed on AWS. It does not provide SQL access to S3 objects.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAmazon CloudWatch
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudWatch does not give users the ability to use standard SQL to query data.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAmazon Athena
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Athena is an interactive query service that makes it easy to use standard SQL to analyze data in Amazon S3. Athena is serverless, so there is no infrastructure to manage. You pay only for the queries that you run./ppFor more information about Athena, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/what-is.html"What is Amazon Athena?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pAmazon RDS
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon RDS does not give users the ability to query S3 data directly.

question_content: pA company is hosting a website on an Amazon EC2 instance that runs in a public subnet inside a VPC. The company uses Amazon CloudWatch Logs for web server log analysis./p  pA SysOps administrator has installed and configured the CloudWatch Logs agent on the EC2 instance and has confirmed that the agent is running. However, logs are not showing up in CloudWatch Logs./p  pWhich solution will resolve this issue?

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the EC2 instance security group rules to allow inbound traffic on port 80.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The inbound security group rules will not affect the ability for the CloudWatch Logs agent to communicate with the CloudWatch Logs endpoint./ppFor more information about how to troubleshoot the CloudWatch Logs agent, see a   href="https://aws.amazon.com/premiumsupport/knowledge-center/push-log-data-cloudwatch-awslogs/"Why can't I push log data to CloudWatch Logs with the awslogs agent?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an IAM user that has the proper permissions for CloudWatch Logs. Create an IAM instance profile, and associate it with the IAM user. Associate the instance profile with the EC2 instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. It is not possible to associate an IAM user with an EC2 instance profile./ppFor more information about how to troubleshoot the CloudWatch Logs agent, see a   href="https://aws.amazon.com/premiumsupport/knowledge-center/push-log-data-cloudwatch-awslogs/"Why can't I push log data to CloudWatch Logs with the awslogs agent?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an IAM role that has the proper permissions for CloudWatch Logs. Create an IAM instance profile, and associate it with the IAM role. Associate the instance profile with the EC2 instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The CloudWatch Logs agent requires access to AWS credentials with the appropriate permissions so that it can send API calls to CloudWatch Logs. The recommended actions are to create an IAM role that has the appropriate permissions and to associate that role with the EC2 instance by using an EC2 instance profile./ppFor more information about how to use an IAM role to grant permissions to applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_switch-role-ec2.html"Using an IAM role to grant permissions to applications running on Amazon EC2 instances/a.  /ppFor more information about how to use EC2 instance profiles, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_switch-role-ec2_instance-profiles.html"Using instance profiles/a. /ppFor more information about how to set up an IAM role for Amazon EC2 to use CloudWatch Logs, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/QuickStartEC2Instance.html#running-ec2-step-1"Step 1: Configure your IAM role or user for CloudWatch Logs/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the VPC's network ACL rules for the public subnet to allow inbound traffic on port 80.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The inbound network ACL rules will not affect the ability for the CloudWatch Logs agent to communicate with the CloudWatch Logs endpoint./ppFor more information how to troubleshoot the CloudWatch Logs agent, see a   href="https://aws.amazon.com/premiumsupport/knowledge-center/push-log-data-cloudwatch-awslogs/"Why can't I push log data to CloudWatch Logs with the awslogs agent?/a

question_content: pA SysOps administrator is receiving alerts related to high CPU utilization of a Memcached-based Amazon ElastiCache cluster./p  pWhich remediation steps should be taken to resolve this issue? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd a larger Amazon EBS volume to the ElastiCache cluster nodes.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached is a Memcached-compatible service that makes it easy to set up, manage, and scale a distributed in-memory data store or cache environment in the cloud. Users cannot set volume size in this service./ppFor more information about the options that you can change in Memcached, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/ParameterGroups.html"Configuring engine parameters using parameter groups/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd a load balancer to route traffic to the ElastiCache cluster.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. No load balancer is needed for Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached. The client connects to a single cluster endpoint and gets configuration information about other nodes. When nodes are added or removed, the client reconfigures itself to use the most current set of nodes./ppFor more information about scaling for ElastiCache for Memcached, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/Scaling.html"Scaling ElastiCache for Memcached clusters/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd additional worker nodes to the ElastiCache cluster.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Additional nodes will provide more capacity for the cluster. The amount of data that an application must process is seldom static. It increases and decreases as a business grows or experiences normal fluctuations in demand. If a company self-manages its cache, the company needs to provision sufficient hardware for demand peaks, which can be expensive. The company can use Amazon ElastiCache so that the cluster can scale to meet current demand./ppFor more information about scaling for ElastiCache for Memcached, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/Scaling.html"Scaling ElastiCache for Memcached clusters/a. /ppFor more information about node management in an ElastiCache for Memcached cluster, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/CacheNodes.html"Managing nodes/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Auto Scaling group for the ElastiCache cluster.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. No Auto Scaling groups are needed for Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached. The client connects to a single cluster endpoint and gets configuration information about other nodes. When nodes are added or removed, the client reconfigures itself to use the most current set of nodes./ppFor more information about scaling for ElastiCache for Memcached, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/Scaling.html"Scaling ElastiCache for Memcached clusters/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pVertically scale the ElastiCache cluster by changing the node type.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. If the node type is too small to meet demand, you can replace the cluster with a new cluster that is made up of nodes with a more robust instance type. The addition of larger or smaller instance types is called vertical scaling./ppFor more about the steps to perform vertical scaling, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/Scaling.html#Scaling.Memcached.Vertically"Scaling ElastiCache for Memcached vertically/a.

question_content: pA company has received a notification in its AWS Health Dashboard that one of its Amazon EBS-backed Amazon EC2 instances is on hardware that is scheduled for maintenance. The instance runs a critical production workload that must be available during normal business hours./ppWhich step will ensure that the instance maintenance does not produce an outage?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure an AWS Lambda function to automatically start the instance if it is stopped.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution will not prevent an outage. It will reduce the length of the outage, but an outage of a critical production system still will occur at an unplanned time.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of the instance and use the AMI to launch a new instance after the existing instance is retired.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. There is no concern about the AMI. The concern is a planned maintenance activity on the underlying AWS hardware that supports the instance. This solution does not prevent the maintenance of the existing instance and does not control when that maintenance will occur. If the instance in the scenario were an instance store-backed volume, then this solution would be possible. However, the scenario refers to an EBS-backed volume.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable termination protection on the EC2 instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Termination protection prevents the accidental termination of resources by the user, but it does not prevent AWS from performing maintenance of underlying hardware./ppFor more information about termination protection and how to terminate instances, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/terminating-instances.html"Terminate your instance/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pStop and start the EC2 instance during a maintenance window outside of normal business hours.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Usually, Amazon EC2 maintenance is a live update to minimize customer impact. Sometimes, however, a live update is not possible. In these cases, a scheduled maintenance event is needed. When an EBS-backed instance that is scheduled for a maintenance event is stopped and restarted, AWS will restart the instance on different hardware that does not require maintenance./ppFor more information about Health Dashboard, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/getting-started-phd.html" Getting started with the AWS Health Dashboard - Your account health/a.

question_content: pA company developed a tagging strategy to define a tag list and its values. The company's SysOps administrator is setting up the tagging strategy for all of the company's AWS Organizations organizational units (OUs)./ppThe company's financial analyst discovers that tags that are applied to some of the resources do not comply with the tagging strategy. The SysOps administrator must implement a solution that can provide a notification for each tag placement that fails to comply with the tag policy./ppWhich solution meets these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS tag policies enforcement to identify noncompliant tags.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Tag policies enforcement prevents noncompliance with the tag policy for new resources that are provisioned. It does not report the resources that are not already tagged according to the policy. The question asks for a notification, not remediation.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Resource Groups Tag Editor to view all noncompliant tags.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Tag Editor is used to search for resources and edit tags. Tag Editor can match tags and values, but it cannot match the absence of a specified set of values.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the required-tags AWS Config managed rule to identify noncompliant tags.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The required-tags managed rule will report on resources that are not tagged according to the definitions that are set within the AWS Config rule. However, the rule is not connected to the tag policy that is set on the organization level.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon EventBridge to monitor for noncompliant tags.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Amazon EventBridge can check for noncompliant resources according to the organization policy that is in place. You can use EventBridge to monitor when noncompliant tags are introduced./ppFor more information about how to monitor noncompliant tags, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_tag-policies-cwe.html" Using CloudWatch Events to monitor noncompliant tags/a.

question_content: pA VPC is connected to a company data center by a VPN. An Amazon EC2 instance with the IP address 172.31.16.139 is within a private subnet of the VPC. A SysOps administrator issued a ping command to the EC2 instance from an on-premises computer with the IP address 203.0.113.12 and did not receive an acknowledgment. VPC Flow Logs were enabled and showed the following:/pp class="aws-mono" style="margin-top:1em;"span style="white-space:nowrap;"2 123456789010 eni-1235b8ca 203.0.113.12 172.31.16.139 0 0 1 4 336 1432917027 1432917142 ACCEPT OK/span/pp class="aws-mono" style="margin-top:1em;"span style="white-space:nowrap;"2 123456789010 eni-1235b8ca 172.31.16.139 203.0.113.12 0 0 1 4 336 1432917094 1432917142 REJECT OK /span/pp style="margin-top:1em;"Which action will resolve the issue?

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the EC2 security group rules to allow inbound traffic from the on-premises computer.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The first Flow Logs line shows that the inbound traffic is successful, so there is no need to change the inbound security group.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the EC2 security group rules to allow outbound traffic to the on-premises computer.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The first Flow Logs line shows that the inbound traffic is successful. Because security groups are stateful, the return trip from the instance, will also be successful.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the VPC network ACL rules to allow inbound traffic from the on-premises computer.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The first Flow Logs line shows that the inbound is packets succeeds, so there is not a problem with the inbound connectivity.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the VPC network ACL rules to allow outbound traffic to the on-premises computer.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. For the example of a ping from your home computer IP address 203.0.113.12 to 172.31.16.139: The security group's inbound rules allow Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) traffic, but the outbound rules do not allow ICMP traffic. Because security groups are stateful, the response ping from your instance is allowed. The network ACL permits inbound ICMP traffic but does not permit outbound ICMP traffic. Because network ACLs are stateless, the response ping is dropped./ppFor more information about flow log records, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs-records-examples.html"Flow log record examples/a. /ppFor more information about network ACLs and security groups, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Security.html"Internetwork traffic privacy in Amazon VPC/a.

question_content: pA SysOps administrator has set up an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to provide an alert when a specific Amazon EC2 instance's CPU utilization is more than 60%. The CloudWatch alarm is configured as follows:/pulliDatapoints to Alarm: 3/liliPeriod: 5 minutes/liliEvaluation Periods: 3/liliEvaluation Range: 5/liliTreatment of missing data points: not breaching/li/ulpThe CPU utilization of the EC2 instance is sustained above 65% in the time frame between 07:00 and 14:00. The SysOps administrator stops the EC2 instance at 07:09 and restarts the EC2 instance at 07:16. The EC2 instance resumes its CPU utilization of more than 65%./ppAt 07:40, what is the status of the alarm?

answer_choices.choice_content: pINSUFFICIENT_DATA
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The alarm will be in ALARM state. The INSUFFICIENT_DATA state means that the alarm has just started, the metric is not available, or not enough data is available for the metric to determine the alarm state.

answer_choices.choice_content: pERROR
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. There is no ERROR state.

answer_choices.choice_content: pOK
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The alarm will be in ALARM state. The OK state means that the designated metric or expression is within the defined threshold.

answer_choices.choice_content: pALARM
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. There are three possible states of a CloudWatch alarm: OK, ALARM, and INSUFFICIENT_DATA. There are enough data points to determine that the state should be ALARM between 07:26 and 07:40, even though there were missing data points when the EC2 instance was stopped./ppThe alarm breaches its threshold at 07:05, 07:21, 07:26, 07:31, and 07:36. Two gaps exist at 07:10 and 07:15 as the EC2 instance was in a stopped state. The Datapoints to Alarm and Evaluation Periods both are set to 3, and the periods that are evaluated as not breaching effectively ignore the missing data points. The result is three consecutive datapoints that are evaluated as ALARM. These datapoints are 07:05, 07:21, and 07:26. Therefore, the alarm will activate at 07:26./ppFor more information about CloudWatch alarms and relevant alarm parameters, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/AlarmThatSendsEmail.html"Using Amazon CloudWatch alarms/a.

question_content: pA SysOps administrator has restored an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume from an EBS snapshot. The new EBS volume initially experienced high latency that resolved over time./ppWhat can the SysOps administrator do to avoid this latency in the future?

answer_choices.choice_content: pDeactivate encryption during the restore.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Whether the volume is encrypted or not, the storage block must be pulled down from Amazon S3 and must be written to the volume before the data can be accessed.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRestore to a different AWS Region.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The Region does not affect the latency of the data retrieval.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRestore to a larger volume with Provisioned IOPS.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Although a volume with higher I/O can perform better, the storage block must be pulled down from Amazon S3 and must be written to the volume before the data can be accessed.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSelect the EBS fast snapshot restore feature.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Restored snapshots require initialization. For EBS volumes that are created from snapshots, the storage blocks must be pulled down from Amazon S3 and must be written to the volume before the data can be accessed. This preliminary action takes time and can cause a significant increase in the latency of I/O operations the first time each block is accessed. Volume performance is achieved after all blocks have been downloaded and written to the volume./ppTo avoid this initial performance decline in a production environment, the following options are available:/pulliForce the immediate initialization of the entire volume./liliActivate fast snapshot restore on a snapshot to ensure that the EBS volumes that are created from it are fully initialized at creation and instantly deliver all of their provisioned performance./li/ulpFor more information about the EBS fast snapshot restore feature, seea  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-fast-snapshot-restore.html"  Amazon EBS fast snapshot restore/a./ppFor more information about how to initialize EBS volumes, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-initialize.html" Initialize Amazon EBS volumes/a.

question_content: pA company is running a site on Amazon EC2 instances. The application stores data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance and has implemented read caching by using an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis (cluster mode enabled) cluster to improve read times. An event is happening over the weekend, and a SysOps administrator expects website traffic to triple./p  pWhat can be done to ensure improved read times for users during the event?

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd shards to the existing Redis cluster.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Users can increase read and write capacity by adding shards (node groups) to a Redis (cluster mode enabled) cluster (replication group). Although the use of a Multi-AZ deployment is a best practice of the AWS Well-Architected Framework, it does not improve general performance./ppFor more information about ElastiCache for Redis, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/UserGuide/scaling-redis-cluster-mode-enabled.html#redis-cluster-resharding-online"What is Amazon ElastiCache for Redis?/a /ppFor more information about cluster mode of ElastiCache for Redis, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/Replication.Redis-RedisCluster.html"Replication: Redis (Cluster Mode Disabled) vs. Redis (Cluster Mode Enabled)/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pOffload static data to Amazon S3.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution will not improve read times because the application cannot access Amazon S3 as quickly as it can access ElastiCache for Redis.

answer_choices.choice_content: pLaunch a second Multi-AZ Redis cluster.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A second cluster would require changes to the application before read times could improve. A Multi-AZ deployment of ElastiCache for Redis will improve availability, but it will not improve performance.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon RDS Multi-AZ.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A switch to Amazon RDS Multi-AZ will improve availability, but it will not improve performance.

question_content: pA company is launching a new workload. The workload will run on Amazon EC2 instances in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group./p  pThe company needs to maintain different versions of the EC2 configurations. The company also needs the Auto Scaling group to automatically scale to maintain CPU utilization of 60%./p  pHow can a SysOps administrator meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the Auto Scaling group to use a launch configuration with a target tracking scaling policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Launch configurations do not support versioning.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the Auto Scaling group to use a launch configuration with a simple scaling policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Launch configurations do not support versioning.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the Auto Scaling group to use a launch template with a target tracking scaling policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Multiple versions of launch templates can be maintained. For example, you can create a default template that defines common configuration parameters and allow the other parameters to be specified as part of another version of the same template. In addition to the features of EC2 Auto Scaling that you can configure by using launch templates, you can use newer features of Amazon EC2. The target tracking scaling policy gives users the ability to increase or decrease the current capacity of the group based on a target value for a specific metric./ppFor more information about launch templates, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/LaunchTemplates.html"Launch templates/a. /ppFor more information about target tracking scaling policies, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scaling-target-tracking.html"Target tracking scaling policies for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the Auto Scaling group to use a launch template with a simple scaling policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The simple scaling policy does not maintain a metric at a certain threshold. It increases or decreases the current capacity of the group based on a single scaling adjustment./ppFor more information about scaling policy types, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scale-based-on-demand.html#as-scaling-types"Dynamic scaling policy types/a. /pp

question_content: pAn application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Auto Scaling group that terminates unhealthy instances. The Auto Scaling group is configured to determine the health status of EC2 instances by using both EC2 status checks and ALB health checks. The development team wants to analyze the unhealthy instances before termination./ppWhat should the SysOps administrator do to accomplish this?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the ALB health check to restart instances instead of terminating them.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution is not a feature of an ALB. This solution also would not give the development team the ability to analyze the instances and learn about what is causing the instances to become unhealthy.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure an AWS Lambda function to take a snapshot of all instances before they are terminated.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution is partially correct, but it is not complete. It does not provide the active running instance for diagnosis.

answer_choices.choice_content: pImplement Amazon EventBridge to capture lifecycle events and invoke an AWS Lambda function for remediation.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution would still terminate the instance without providing an instance for diagnosis.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hook to pause instance termination after the instance has been removed from service.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. With lifecycle hooks, you can perform custom actions by pausing instances as an Auto Scaling group launches or terminates them. When an instance is paused, the instance remains in a wait state until you complete the lifecycle action by using the complete-lifecycle-action command or the CompleteLifecycleAction operation, or until the timeout period ends (1 hour by default)./ppFor more information about how to pause an instance in an Auto Scaling group, see a   href="https://aws.amazon.com/premiumsupport/knowledge-center/auto-scaling-delay-termination/"How do I delay Auto Scaling termination of unhealthy Amazon EC2 instances so I can troubleshoot them?/a /ppFor more information about lifecycle hooks, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/lifecycle-hooks.html"Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks/a.

question_content: pA SysOps administrator has set up a new Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. The desired capacity is 20 instances during the day, but a job changes the desired capacity to 10 instances overnight./ppWhen CPU utilization is below 20% across the instances, a single instance must be automatically removed every 400 seconds when the condition applies./ppWhat is the MOST operationally efficient way to configure this change?

answer_choices.choice_content: pSend an SMS message through Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) whenever CPU utilization is below 20%. Access the AWS Management Console to reduce the Auto Scaling group's desired capacity by one instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The solution should be automated with a scaling policy to meet the requirement for operational efficiency.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon CloudWatch alarm and a target tracking scaling policy that removes an instance when CPU utilization is below 20%.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Target tracking scaling policies set a target value, not a minimum value as the questions describes.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon CloudWatch alarm and a step scaling policy that removes an instance when CPU utilization is below 20%.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Step scaling policies apply a percentage of instances to change. But a percentage that equates to a single instance at night would equate to two instances during the day, which does not meet the requirement.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon CloudWatch alarm and a simple scaling policy that removes an instance when CPU utilization is below 20%.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Simple scaling policies can be configured to take action when a CloudWatch alarm is active. Simple scaling policies can be configured to scale in or out, and they repeat the action during a set time interval. These policies scale a fixed number of instances./ppFor more information about step scaling policies and simple scaling policies, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scaling-simple-step.html"Step and simple scaling policies for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling/a.

question_content: pA company is running a media streaming website that serves users around the world. The website is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances that are behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB)./p  pThe company is running its infrastructure redundantly across two AWS Regions. Each Region contains its own separate copy of the website infrastructure. If one Region becomes unusable due to an application error, the company wants to automatically fail over traffic to the other Region./p  pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon Route 53 to set up DNS failover with a latency-based routing policy. Create an alias record with the same name and type for each ALB in each Region. Ensure that Evaluate Health Target is set to Yes for each record.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Amazon Route 53 is used to create DNS failover for active-active AWS Region architectures. When a resource becomes unavailable, Route 53 can detect that the resource is unhealthy and stop including the resource when responding to queries./ppIn active-active failover, all the records that have the same name, the same type (such as A or AAAA), and the same routing policy (such as weighted or latency) are active unless Route 53 considers them unhealthy. Route 53 can respond to a DNS query using any healthy record./ppActive-active failover returns multiple resources to DNS queries. When one resource is unhealthy, Route 53 fails over to another resource./ppFor more information about how to set up DNS failover with Route 53, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-how-to.html"Task list for configuring DNS failover/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a health check for the ALB in each Region by using Elastic Load Balancing health checks. Set up DNS failover with a latency-based routing policy for the ALB. Ensure that Evaluate Health Target is set to Yes.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Application Load Balancers do allow for the creation of health checks, but the health checks are for the backend resources where the load balancer is sending traffic. A health check for the load balancer cannot be set up from the Application Load Balancer. Also, Application Load Balancers can distribute traffic only within a Region. There is no latency-based routing available from the Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic across Regions.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon Route 53 to set up DNS failover with a simple routing policy. Create an alias record with the same name for each ALB in each Region. Ensure that Evaluate Health Target is set to Yes for each record.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. If the simple routing policy is chosen in the Route 53 console, multiple records that have the same name and type cannot be created. Therefore, the necessary records for DNS failover cannot be set up with multiple active Regions./ppFor more information about routing policies, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy.html"Choosing a routing policy/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a health check for the ALB by using Amazon CloudWatch monitoring. Set up a CloudWatch alarm to launch a DNS failover with an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy whenever the ALB becomes unhealthy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudWatch cannot determine where to deliver incoming traffic based on health checks. CloudWatch alarms can be set up to monitor the health of AWS resources, but CloudWatch does not have the ability to perform DNS failover between Regions.

question_content: pA real estate company is deploying a legacy web application on Amazon EC2 instances. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. answer_choices.choice_content: pReplace the DB instance with Amazon ElastiCache.

question_content: pA company is hosting a web application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A target tracking scaling policy might be useful, but it will not ensure that the Auto Scaling group always has 10 instances. With a target tracing policy, a specific metric to target must be chosen. The target to track cannot be set to 10.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRemove the Auto Scaling group. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to invoke an AWS Lambda function to launch a new instance when an unhealthy instance is detected.

A steady-state Auto Scaling group can be configured by setting the minimum number of instances, the maximum number of instances, and the desired capacity to the same number. If an instance becomes unhealthy and the Auto Scaling group drops below the minimum number of 10, a new instance will launch automatically. With the maximum number of instances and the desired capacity also set to 10, the Auto Scaling group always will have 10 instances./ppFor more information about Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/what-is-amazon-ec2-auto-scaling.html"What is Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling?/a /pp

answer_choices.choice_content: pRemove the Auto Scaling group. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke an AWS Lambda function to launch a new instance when an unhealthy instance is detected.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The Lambda function is not needed. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can meet the requirements without forcing the company to maintain the code for the Lambda function.

question_content: pA SysOps administrator is managing an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the RDS instance to be a Multi-AZ deployment.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. In the case of Multi-AZ deployments, failover occurs automatically. Additionally, the endpoint that applications use to access the database does not change./ppYou can change an RDS DB instance to Multi-AZ without interfering with the normal operation of the database. However, you can experience a performance impact during the conversion. Therefore, it is best to make this change during periods of low activity./ppFor more information about high availability for Amazon RDS, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.html"High availability (Multi-AZ) for Amazon RDS/a.

question_content: pA company's Amazon EC2 costs have stayed the same, but the company's Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) costs have increased recently. answer_choices.choice_content: pCheck that the default data lifecycle policy is selected.

Automation of snapshot and AMI management helps you accomplish the following:/pulliProtect valuable data by enforcing a regular backup schedule./liliCreate standardized AMIs that can be refreshed at regular intervals./liliRetain backups as required by auditors or internal compliance./liliReduce storage costs by deleting outdated backups./liliCreate disaster recovery backup policies that backup data to isolated accounts./li/ulpFor more information about Amazon DLM, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/snapshot-lifecycle.html" Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager/a.

question_content: pA company recently adopted a compliance policy that requires a multi-Region presence for all data that is stored for a project. The data consists of CSV files and JSON files. question_content: pA telecommunications company is developing a new application. A third-party vendor is passing observability log files through Amazon EventBridge to invoke an AWS Lambda function. The Lambda function processes the log files and then writes the results to an Amazon S3 bucket. In testing, EventBridge is sending all log files immediately to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) dead-letter queue instead of attempting any retry./ppWhich step should the SysOps administrator take to troubleshoot this issue?

answer_choices.choice_content: pValidate that the processing jobs in the Lambda function do not regularly exceed the socket's timeout.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Even if all jobs timed out, that would not cause EventBridge to immediately send the log files to a dead-letter queue. The job was received successfully, but it was not processed completely.

answer_choices.choice_content: pValidate that the S3 bucket does not have any Deny policies that prevent the Lambda function from writing results.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. While Deny policies would prevent the Lambda function from successfully completing the write task, they would not affect the ability of EventBridge to send the log files to Lambda.

answer_choices.choice_content: pValidate that the EventBridge event bus has permissions to the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) for EventBridge.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Even if the architecture used encrypted transmissions (which is not mentioned in the question), the fact that the event bus can write to the dead-letter queue indicates that permissions to the AWS KMS functions already have been applied to the event bus./ppFor more information about AWS KMS permissions when writing to encrypted queues, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eventbridge-getting-set-up.html"Getting started with Amazon EventBridge/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pValidate that the IAM role that is assigned to the EventBridge event bus has permissions to the Lambda function.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Amazon EventBridge has an automatic retry function for when an event is not received. By default, EventBridge retries sending the event for 24 hours and up to 185 times with an exponential backoff and jitter, or randomized delay. If an event is not delivered before all retry attempts are exhausted, the event is dropped and EventBridge does not continue to process it. To avoid losing events after they fail to be delivered to a target, configure a dead-letter queue and send all failed events to it for processing later./ppIn this scenario, the event is going straight to the dead-letter queue without any attempts to redeliver. This scenario can happen when errors result from missing permissions to a target, or when a target resource no longer exists. For events that go directly to the dead-letter queue, the first step of troubleshooting is to check the associated IAM permissions./ppFor more information about EventBridge event retry policies, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/rule-dlq.html" Event retry policy and using dead-letter queues/a./ppFor more information about how to assign the correct IAM access to EventBridge when sending to Lambda, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eventbridge-troubleshooting.html#lam-function-not-invoked" Troubleshooting Amazon EventBridge/a.

question_content: pA company has a development team that performs testing on AWS. The costs of this testing must remain within budget. Only a defined subset of AWS services and resources should be available for testing./ppWhich solution will meet these requirements?

The costs associated with testing and other innovations can be managed. AWS services allow you to monitor your spending and implement limits around the AWS services that can be provisioned./ppFor more information about AWS Budgets, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/budgets-create.html"Creating a budget/a. /ppFor more information about how to use AWS Service Catalog to implement portfolios of preapproved products for provisioning, see a   href="https://aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/features/"AWS Service Catalog features/a. /ppFor more information about how to tag AWS resources, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws_tagging.html"Tagging AWS resources/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRequest that the development team use only the permitted AWS services and resources.
