answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Asking the developers to monitor costs and the AWS services and resources used does not meet the requirements. Tagging defines additional metadata for a resource. To monitor costs, tags need to be activated as cost allocation tags to be used by Cost Explorer and AWS Budgets.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Cost Explorer to monitor only the cost of the subset of AWS services and resources allowed for testing. Monitor these costs starting from the day the budget is available for consumption until the date when the costs exceed the budget.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution does not enforce AWS service restrictions and cost monitoring. Monitoring the budget in this way does not provide a mechanism to determine if any net new spend is a result of the testing or related to other workloads.

question_content: pA company's SysOps administrator needs to report on Amazon EC2 instance costs. The report must organize costs by the name and the department of the developer who launched the instances. The company uses a single AWS account./ppWhat is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a separate AWS account for each developer. Use a separate AWS Region for each department. Summarize the invoices by developer name and department.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. It would be operationally inefficient to create a separate AWS account for each developer and summarize the invoices manually.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a separate AWS account for each developer. Create an organization in AWS Organizations for each department. Summarize the invoices by developer name and department.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. It would be operationally inefficient to create a separate AWS account for each developer and summarize the invoices manually.

answer_choices.choice_content: pImplement tags that identify the developer and department for all instances. Enable cost allocation tagging in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console. Run reports from the Billing and Cost Management console.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use tags to organize your resources. You can use cost allocation tags to track your AWS costs on a detailed level. After you activate cost allocation tags, AWS uses the cost allocation tags to organize your resource costs on your cost allocation report to make it easier for you to categorize and track your AWS costs. You must activate tags before they can appear in Cost Explorer or on a cost allocation report./ppFor more information about cost allocation tags, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/cost-alloc-tags.html"Using Cost Allocation Tags/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd the department and environment information to the instance metadata of each instance when it is launched. Include the metadata in reports from the AWS Billing and Cost Management console.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. EC2 metadata is generated when an instance is launched. This data records the configuration of the instance. This data cannot provide the information that is described in the scenario./ppFor more information about metadata, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-metadata.html"Instance metadata and user data/a.

question_content: pA SysOps administrator uses the aws s3 ls s3://bucketname command and receives an empty response for an Amazon S3 bucket that needs to be deleted. When the SysOps administrator runs the aws s3 rb s3://bucketname command on the S3 bucket, Amazon S3 returns a BucketNotEmpty error and does not remove the S3 bucket./ppWhy is the SysOps administrator unable to delete the S3 bucket?

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe S3 bucket has MFA delete enabled.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. When you work with S3 Versioning in S3 buckets, you can add another layer of security by configuring an S3 bucket to enable MFA (multi-factor authentication) delete. When you perform this task, the S3 bucket owner must include two forms of authentication in any request to delete a version or change the versioning state of the S3 bucket. MFA delete applies to deletion of objects in an S3 bucket, but MFA delete does not apply to deletion of the S3 bucket itself./ppFor more information about MFA delete, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MultiFactorAuthenticationDelete.html"Configuring MFA delete/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe S3 bucket has S3 Versioning enabled.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. When S3 Versioning is enabled, a simple delete request cannot permanently delete an object. Instead, Amazon S3 inserts a delete marker in the S3 bucket, and that marker becomes the current version of the object with a new version ID. Even though the aws s3 ls command shows no output, the original file still exists. Before the S3 bucket can be removed, you must delete all objects that have a delete marker by using their version IDs./ppFor more information about S3 delete markers, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/ManagingDelMarkers.html"Managing delete markers/a. /ppFor more information about the deletion of S3 buckets, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/delete-bucket.html"Deleting a bucket/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe S3 bucket is storing files in S3 Glacier.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Although there is a delay in object retrieval from S3 Glacier, the deletion of objects in S3 Glacier does not impose a delay. Therefore, this reason does not explain the error./ppFor more information about how to delete archives from S3 Glacier, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonglacier/latest/dev/deleting-an-archive.html"Deleting an Archive in Amazon S3 Glacier/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe S3 bucket has default server-side encryption enabled.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Default encryption on an S3 bucket does not affect whether an empty S3 bucket can be deleted./ppFor more information about S3 default bucket encryption, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/default-bucket-encryption.html"Enabling Amazon S3 default bucket encryption/a.

question_content: pA financial company runs a regulated web application. The company uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy the application. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group./p  pFor compliance, the company must send a complete copy of all regulated data on the attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to an Amazon S3 bucket before an EC2 instance is terminated. In testing, some EC2 instances are terminated before the data can be completely copied./p  pWhat can a SysOps administrator do to resolve this problem in normal operating conditions?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks to put the instances into a Terminating:Wait status before the instances are terminated. When the copy is complete, use the complete-lifecycle-action command.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The implementation of functions on a terminating instance can take time that must be accounted for as part of the EC2 lifecycle. EC2 Auto Scaling allows for a lifecycle hook to be applied to an instance as it begins to be decommissioned. The lifecycle hook puts the instance into a wait state (Terminating:Wait). During the default timeout period, exit functions can be run on the instance. When these functions are complete, a change in the status to Terminating:Proceed allows the termination function to finish./ppFor more information about EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/lifecycle-hooks.html"Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks/a. /ppFor more information about how to run code before terminating an EC2 Auto Scaling instance, see a   href="https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/infrastructure-and-automation/run-code-before-terminating-an-ec2-auto-scaling-instance/"Run code before terminating an EC2 Auto Scaling instance/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse S3 Lifecycle hooks to enable the CreateMultipartUpload API feature with S3 Transfer Acceleration. When the copy is complete, use the complete-lifecycle-action command.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The CreateMultipartUpload feature would allow objects that fail to completely load during the first attempt to retry parts that had not yet loaded. In this case, the interruption would be due to the termination of the EBS volume, so the data that needed to load would no longer be available. This operation would not complete because the source would no longer exist. S3 Transfer Acceleration enables fast and secure transfers of files over long distances between a client and an S3 bucket. It is not meant for use with EC2 instances in the same AWS Region.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpdate the CloudFormation stack template, and set the DisableApiTermination property to true for the EC2 instances. Run an update-stack operation.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. It is useful to disable API termination to prevent an instance from being terminated accidentally or without authorization. In this case, the SysOps administrator wants the instance to terminate automatically. By setting the DisableApiTermination property to true, the command to initiate the termination sequence would be denied. A change of the property to false would allow the sequence to begin but would do nothing to increase the amount of time that is available to complete a data copy.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpdate the CloudFormation stack template, and set the AutoEnableIO property to true for the EBS volumes. Run an update-stack operation.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The AutoEnableIO property indicates whether the volume is auto-enabled for I/O operations. By default, Amazon EBS disables I/O to the volume from attached EC2 instances when it determines that a volume's data is potentially inconsistent. A value of true for the AutoEnableIO property would allow the volume to be attached even if consistency issues were detected. None of that solves the problem of data copying.

question_content: pA team is using Amazon EC2 instances to conduct a load test. The instance type and AWS Region are specified in the requirements for the load test and cannot be changed. The EC2 instances use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. As the team is scaling additional instances, the team encounters an InstanceLimitExceeded error./ppWhat can the team do to resolve this error?

answer_choices.choice_content: pIncrease the service quota for Amazon EC2.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Service quotas protect an account from the accidental launch of more instances than is normal for the account. However, when legitimate usage patterns change, the quotas must change to reflect the new patterns./ppYou should know the following about service quotas:/pulliThe different types of service quotas/liliWhen service quotas are a factor/liliWhat happens when service quotas are exceeded/liliWhat to do when encountering a service quota/li/ulpFor more information about service quotas in general, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws_service_limits.html" AWS service quotas/a./ppFor more information about service quotas for EC2 instances, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-resource-limits.html" Amazon EC2 service quotas/a./ppFor more information about service quotas for EC2 instances for Windows, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/WindowsGuide/ec2-resource-limits.html" Amazon EC2 service quotas/a./ppFor more information about what occurs when service quotas are exceeded for EC2 instances, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/troubleshooting-launch.html" Troubleshoot instance launch issues/a./ppFor more information about what occurs when service quotas are exceeded for EC2 instances for Windows, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/WindowsGuide/troubleshooting-launch.html#troubleshooting-launch-limit" Instance limit exceeded/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRun the test in a different Availability Zone.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The service quota is set for each Region. The same error will occur if the test is run in a different Availability Zone.

answer_choices.choice_content: pTerminate the EC2 instance. Relaunch the instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Termination of the instance will not address this issue.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDetach the EBS volume. Relaunch the instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The attachment of an EBS volume will not affect this error message.

question_content: pA SysOps administrator manages an AWS CloudFormation template that provisions Amazon EC2 instances, an Elastic Load Balancer, and Amazon RDS instances. As part of an ongoing transformation project, CloudFormation stacks are being created and deleted continuously. The administrator needs to ensure that the RDS instances continue running after a stack has been deleted./p  pWhich action should be taken to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pEdit the template to remove the RDS resources and update the stack.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The removal of the RDS resources from the stack does not disassociate the existing instances from the stack. Instead, it causes the RDS resources to be deleted when the stack is updated.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable termination protection on the stack.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution prevents deletion of the RDS resources, but it also prevents deletion of all the other resources./ppFor more information about CloudFormation stack protection, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-protect-stacks.html"Protecting a stack from being deleted/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet the DeletionPolicy attribute for RDS resources to Retain in the template.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. This solution protects the RDS resources from deletion when the stack is deleted, and it does not affect the ability to delete the other resources./ppFor more information about the DeletionPolicy attribute, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html"DeletionPolicy attribute/a. /ppFor more information about the other uses of the DeletionPolicy attribute, see a   href="https://aws.amazon.com/premiumsupport/knowledge-center/delete-cf-stack-retain-resources/"How do I retain some of my resources when I delete an AWS CloudFormation stack?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet the deletion-protection parameter on RDS resources.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution prevents the deletion of the entire CloudFormation stack./ppFor more information about how to use termination protection, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-protect-stacks.html"Protecting a stack from being deleted/a.

question_content: pA company has hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances in its environment. The company's security team wants to make sure that all the security patches and critical patches are installed on all the EC2 instances. A SysOps administrator needs to automate this process./p  pHow can the SysOps administrator meet this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: pSchedule an AWS Lambda function that uses AWS Config to retrieve a list of the current software releases that are installed on the EC2 instances. Configure the Lambda function to patch the instances that need the security updates and critical updates.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS Config provides a detailed view of the configuration of AWS resources in an AWS account. It does not give the details of software that is installed on servers./ppFor more information about AWS Config, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/WhatIsConfig.html"What Is AWS Config?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to apply the patches on a schedule. Use a predefined patch baseline that approves all patches that are classified as security updates or critical updates.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Systems Manager Patch Manager automates the process of patching managed instances with security-related updates and other types of updates. You can use Patch Manager to apply patches for operating systems and applications. Patch Manager uses patch baselines, which include rules for auto-approving patches within days of their release, as well as a list of approved and rejected patches. You can install patches on a regular basis by scheduling patching to run as a Systems Manager maintenance window task. You also can install patches individually or to large groups of instances by using EC2 tags./ppFor more information about Patch Manager, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-patch.html"AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager/a.  /ppFor more information about how to patch EC2 servers by using Patch Manager, see a   href="https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/patching-your-windows-ec2-instances-using-aws-systems-manager-patch-manager/"Patching your Windows EC2 instances using AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSchedule an AWS Lambda function that uses Amazon CloudWatch to retrieve a list of the current software releases that are installed on the EC2 instances. Configure the Lambda function to patch the instances that need the security updates and critical updates.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudWatch does not provide a list of AWS resources or a list of software that is installed on EC2 instances./ppFor more information about CloudWatch, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/WhatIsCloudWatch.html"What is Amazon CloudWatch?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the EC2 console to retrieve a list of the current software releases that are installed on the EC2 instances. Add a tag to the EC2 instances that need patch updates. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to patch the instances based upon the tag.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The EC2 console does not have any configuration details or a list of software that is installed on EC2 instances./ppFor more information about Amazon EC2, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ec2/index.html"Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud Documentation/a.

question_content: pA SysOps administrator must run a script on production servers to fix an issue. The company has a policy to block all remote interactive access to production servers./p  pBased on this situation, how should the administrator run the script?

answer_choices.choice_content: pShare and use the Amazon EC2 key pairs to gain access to the servers and run the script.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The use of key pairs would make interactive access possible and would go against the company policy.

answer_choices.choice_content: pPut the script into the user data of the instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. User data scripts run only on the instance initialization.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the script to run as a cron job or scheduled task on the EC2 instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This option does not describe a way to get the cron job or scheduled task to run on the instance.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Systems Manager to run the script.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. With Systems Manager and its feature Session Manager, you can run scripts on a specific system or on groups of systems. This centralized access is controllable through IAM policies. Systems Manager does not require the SSH ports to be open and removes the need to manage bastion hosts./ppFor more information about Systems Manager, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager.html"AWS Systems Manager Session Manager/a.

question_content: pA company runs an image-processing application on a serverless infrastructure. Each processing job runs in a single AWS Lambda invocation. A SysOps administrator is tasked with ensuring there is enough capacity to run 500 simultaneous jobs even if other Lambda functions are being run for other applications. The administrator has already increased service limits within the Region./p  pWhich action should be taken?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure a dead-letter queue to retry any throttled requests.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You could use a dead-letter queue to reprocess jobs that could not run. However, the scenario requires that the jobs run simultaneously. This solution does not meet that requirement./ppFor more information about how to use a dead-letter queue with Lambda, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async.html"Asynchronous invocation/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the memory settings on the Lambda function to allow for 500 parallel runs.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution increases memory and CPU capacity of the Lambda function, but it does not allow for 500 parallel runs.

answer_choices.choice_content: pMove the image-processing logic to AWS Step Functions.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Step Functions can orchestrate Lambda functions, but it does not provide an increase in parallel runs./ppFor more information about Step Functions, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/welcome.html"What is AWS Step Functions?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet the reserved concurrency for the image-processing Lambda function to 500.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Lambda uses quotas to determine how many concurrent runs are allowed for the AWS account. However, if different functions are competing for this number, you can further define concurrent runs./ppFor more information about concurrency, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-concurrency.html"Managing concurrency for a Lambda function/a. /ppFor more information about Lambda quotas, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html"Lambda quotas/a.

question_content: pA company is requesting build statistics from its development teams. These development teams use AWS CodePipeline with AWS CodeCommit, AWS CodeBuild, and AWS CodeDeploy for the continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) process./ppWhich solution creates this report with the LEAST amount of effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: pImplement the report in a static web page hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure CodePipeline to place all build events into an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure the web page to read from the Kinesis data stream, process the events, and display on a dashboard.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodePipeline cannot use Kinesis data streams to communicate build events.

answer_choices.choice_content: pImplement the report in an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard. Configure the dashboard to graph metrics such as total builds, successful builds, failed builds, and average build time for the application.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. CodeBuild monitors functions and reports metrics through CloudWatch. These metrics include the number of total builds, number of failed builds, number of successful builds, and the duration of builds. You can use the CodeBuild console or the CloudWatch console to monitor metrics for CodeBuild./ppFor more information about CodeBuild metrics, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/monitoring-metrics.html"Monitoring CodeBuild metrics/a. /ppFor more information about how to add a graph to a CloudWatch dashboard, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/add_remove_graph_dashboard.html"Add or remove a graph from a CloudWatch dashboard/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pImplement the report in a web page hosted on Amazon EC2. Configure CodePipeline to put all build events into an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure the web page to read metrics from the table, process them, and display on a dashboard.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodePipeline cannot directly push events into a DynamoDB table without a custom function.

answer_choices.choice_content: pImplement the report in an Amazon QuickSight dashboard. Configure CodeBuild and CodeDeploy to insert build and deploy events into a table in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster. Configure QuickSight to read from this table.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeBuild and CodeDeploy cannot insert events into an Aurora table without a custom function./ppFor more information about Aurora, see a   href="https://aws.amazon.com/rds/aurora"Amazon Aurora/a.

question_content: pA company hosts a data processing application on a fleet of 50 Amazon EC2 instances that are all running from the same Amazon Linux 2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI). Each instance is tagged with the application name./ppA new operating system security patch needs to be applied to all 50 instances. A SysOps administrator must apply the patch to the instances by using automation tools. The SysOps administrator also must automate future patching with as little human interaction as possible. After the patches are applied, a report must be generated to show which instances are in compliance with the latest security patch./ppWhich solution meets these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to create a patch baseline for the EC2 instances that share the application tag. Use the Patch now option in Patch Manager to patch all the instances. Set up a maintenance window for the future patches to be applied.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Patch Manager automates the process of patching managed instances with security-related updates and other types of updates. Patch Manager can apply patches for operating systems and applications./ppPatch Manager uses patch baselines, which include rules for auto-approving patches within days of their release, as well as a list of approved and rejected patches. You can install patches on a regular basis by scheduling patching to run as a Systems Manager maintenance window task. You can also install patches individually or install patches to large groups of instances by using EC2 tags./ppFor the first round of patches to be installed right away, you can use the Patch now option in Patch Manager. You also can run on-demand patching operations from the Systems Manager console./ppFor future patches, you can create a maintenance window in which security patches should be applied. Patch Manager also creates a report that shows which instances are in compliance with the latest approved security patch./ppFor more information about Patch Manager, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/sysman-patch-working.html"Working with Patch Manager (console)/a. /ppFor more information about Run Command, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/execute-remote-commands.html"AWS Systems Manager Run Command/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Systems Manager Run Command to create a patch baseline for the EC2 instances that share the application tag. Use the Patch now option in Run Command to patch all the instances. Set up a maintenance window for the future patches to be applied.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Run Command does not have the Patch now option or the ability to create a patch baseline.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse SSH to connect to all the instances that share the application tag. Run a script that downloads and installs the security patch and then updates a database for the report to be generated from. Repeat these steps every time a new patch is released.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution is a manual process that would require the system operator to use SSH to connect to every instance individually. Therefore, this solution does not meet the automation requirements.

answer_choices.choice_content: pWrite a script to download and install the latest security patch. Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to invoke the script on all the instances that share the application tag. Repeat these steps every time a new patch is released.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Pieces of this process are automated, such as the running of the script with Run Command. However, the script would need to be updated with a manual process for every security patch that is released. Therefore, this solution does not meet the requirement of minimum human interaction for the installation of future security patches.

question_content: pA company has several AWS member accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company has chosen to receive AWS Cost and Usage Reports in its management account and has specified the name of the Amazon S3 bucket in which to store these reports. However, none of the member account owners can view the reports./p  pWhy are the member account owners unable to view the reports?

answer_choices.choice_content: pBucket policies on the S3 bucket in the member accounts need to allow access to the account owner.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Billing reports are delivered to the S3 bucket in the management account, not the member account.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe reports are saved in an S3 bucket that is owned by the management account in the organization.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. When using the consolidated billing feature in Organizations, the Amazon S3 bucket designated to receive the billing reports is owned by the management account. You cannot receive billing reports in an S3 bucket that is owned by a member account. The management account controls access to the S3 bucket that contains the consolidated billing reports./ppFor more information about Organizations, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_introduction.html"What is AWS Organizations?/a /ppFor more information about Billing and Cost Management, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/billing-what-is.html"What is AWS Billing and Cost Management?/a /ppFor more information about consolidated billing for Organizations, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/consolidated-billing.html"Consolidated billing for AWS Organizations/a. /ppFor more information about billing and account activity for consolidated billing in Organizations, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/useconsolidatedbilling-activity.html"Billing and account activity/a. /ppFor more information about Cost and Usage Reports, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cur/latest/userguide/what-is-cur.html"What are AWS Cost and Usage Reports?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe reports can be delivered only to Amazon Athena.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Billing reports are delivered to the S3 bucket in the management account.

answer_choices.choice_content: pVersioning needs to be enabled on the S3 bucket in the member accounts.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Billing reports are delivered to the S3 bucket in the management account. Versioning is not required.

question_content: pA company's audit shows that users have been changing cost-related tags on Amazon EC2 instances after deployment. The company has an organization in AWS Organizations with many AWS accounts./p  pThe company needs a solution to detect the EC2 instances automatically. The solution must require the least possible operational overhead./p  pWhich solution meets these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse service control policies (SCPs) to track EC2 instances that do not have the required tags.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. SCPs do not audit instances for required tags.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon Inspector to run a report to identify EC2 instances that do not have the required tags.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon Inspector is not the right tool because it tests the network accessibility of EC2 instances and the security state of applications that run on those instances.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an AWS Config rule to track EC2 instances that do not have the required tags.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. AWS Config provides managed rules that are used to evaluate whether AWS resources comply with a desired configuration. One of these managed rules is approved-amis-by-tag, and it checks whether running instances are using specified Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) with a specified tag. If an instance does not have at least one of the specified tags, it is labeled NON_COMPLIANT./ppFor more information about AWS managed rules, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config_use-managed-rules.html"AWS Config Managed Rules/a. /ppFor more information about the approved-amis-by-tag managed rule, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/approved-amis-by-tag.html"approved-amis-by-tag/a. /ppFor more information about SCPs, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html"Service control policies/a. /pp

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Well-Architected Tool (AWS WA Tool) to run a report to identify EC2 instances that do not have the required tags.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution can help a single account, but it is not automated.

question_content: pA SysOps administrator implemented the following bucket policy to allow only the corporate IP address range of 54.240.143.0/24 to access objects in an Amazon S3 bucket:/pp class="aws-mono"{/pp class="aws-mono"  "Version": "2012-10-17",/pp class="aws-mono"  "Id": "S3PolicyId1",/pp class="aws-mono"  "Statement": [/pp class="aws-mono"  {/pp class="aws-mono"  "Sid": "S3Allow",/pp class="aws-mono"  "Effect": "Allow",/pp class="aws-mono"  "Principal": "*",/pp class="aws-mono"  "Action": "s3:*",/pp class="aws-mono"  "Resource": [/pp class="aws-mono"  "arn:aws:s3:::examplebucket",/pp class="aws-mono"  "arn:aws:s3:::examplebucket/*"/pp class="aws-mono"  ]/pp class="aws-mono"  },/pp class="aws-mono"  {/pp class="aws-mono"  "Sid": "IPAllow",/pp class="aws-mono"  "Effect": "Allow",/pp class="aws-mono"  "Principal": "*",/pp class="aws-mono"  "Action": "s3:*",/pp class="aws-mono"  "Resource": [/pp class="aws-mono"  "arn:aws:s3:::examplebucket",/pp class="aws-mono"  "arn:aws:s3:::examplebucket/*"/pp class="aws-mono"  ],/pp class="aws-mono"  "Condition": {/pp class="aws-mono"  "NotIpAddress": {/pp class="aws-mono"  "aws:SourceIp": "54.240.143.0/24"/pp class="aws-mono"  }/pp class="aws-mono"  }/pp class="aws-mono"  }/pp class="aws-mono"  ]/pp class="aws-mono"}/pp style="margin-top:10px;"Some employees are reporting that they are able to access the S3 bucket from IP addresses outside the corporate IP address range./ppHow can the administrator address this issue?

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the span class="aws-mono"Condition/span operator to include both span class="aws-mono"NotIpAddress/span and span class="aws-mono"IpAddress/span to prevent unauthorized access to the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution might be used to define a CIDR range to include and a subrange to exclude. However, that functionality is not needed in this scenario.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the span class="aws-mono"Condition/span element from the IAM policy to span class="aws-mono"aws:StringEquals/span instead of span class="aws-mono"aws:SourceIp/span.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The bucket policy needs to enforce access based on the source IP address. Therefore, the span class="aws-mono"aws:SourceIp/span condition key is necessary.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the IAM policy instead of the bucket policy to restrict users from accessing the bucket based on their source IP addresses.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution does not address the issue, which is that unauthorized entities can access the bucket. The administrator can apply the span class="aws-mono"aws:SourceIp/span condition key to the IAM policy, but the condition key would apply only at the user level. To prevent unauthorized access to the entire bucket, the administrator would need to apply the span class="aws-mono"aws:SourceIp/span condition key at the bucket level to allow only certain IP addresses.

answer_choices.choice_content: pChange span class="aws-mono"Effect/span from span class="aws-mono"Allow/spanto span class="aws-mono"Deny/span in the second statement of the policy to deny requests not from the source IP range.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The allow in the first section of this bucket policy is restricted by the second section that adds an explicit deny for connections that are outside the corporate CIDR range. The combination of those two sections provides access, but only from the company range./ppFor more information about condition keys, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/amazon-s3-policy-keys.html" Amazon S3 condition key examples/a./ppFor more information about examples of similar bucket policies, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-bucket-policies.html#example-bucket-policies-use-case-3" Bucket policy examples/a.

question_content: pA company's AWS account users are launching Amazon EC2 instances without required cost allocation tags. A SysOps administrator needs to prevent users within an organization in AWS Organizations from launching new EC2 instances that do not have the required tags. The solution must require the least possible operational overhead./p  pWhich solution meets these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up an AWS Lambda function that will initiate a run instance event and check for the required tags. Configure the function to prevent the launch of EC2 instances if the tags are missing.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A Lambda function can stop instances based on an event trigger from Amazon EC2. However, this approach is more complex and must be run on each individual account.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up an AWS Config rule to monitor for EC2 instances that lack the required tags.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The required-tags AWS Config managed rule can monitor specific tags on resources. However, remediation would require a Lambda function. Also, this solution would need to be configured on each individual account.

answer_choices.choice_content: p Set up a service control policy (SCP) that prevents the launch of EC2 instances that lack the required tags. Attach the SCP to the organization root.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. SCPs can enforce tagging at the account level for specific AWS resources. You can use SCPs for an organizational unit (OU) to prevent the creation of AWS resources that do not have specific tags for all accounts under the OU./ppFor more information about how to use SCPs to require specified tags on objects before their creation, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_example-scps.html#example-require-tag-on-create"Example service control policies/a.  /ppFor more information about best practices for tag policies, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_tag-policies-best-practices.html"Best practices for using tag policies/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to stop any EC2 instances that lack the required tags.br class="t-last-br"
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The setup of a custom metric to monitor tags on resources is a more complex solution. This solution would need to be configured on each individual account.

question_content: pA SysOps administrator needs a secure way to connect to AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) within a VPC. The SysOps administrator must ensure that connections to AWS KMS do not traverse the internet./ppWhat is the MOST secure solution that meets these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse a bastion host to connect to AWS KMS.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A bastion host is a server that provides access to a private network from an external network, such as the internet./ppFor more about bastion hosts, see a  href="https://aws.amazon.com/solutions/implementations/linux-bastion/" Linux Bastion Hosts on AWS/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse a NAT gateway to connect to AWS KMS.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A NAT gateway can be used to connect to the internet from instances within a private subnet in a VPC./ppFor more information about NAT gateways, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html"NAT gateways/a. /pp

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse a VPC gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 to connect to AWS KMS.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The scenario does not require any resources to be accessed through Amazon S3, so there is no need to have a connection through VPC endpoints for Amazon S3. Also, a VPC gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 would not cover other use cases for Amazon DynamoDB, AWS KMS, and other services./ppFor more information about VPC endpoints for Amazon S3, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html" Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse a VPC interface endpoint to connect to AWS KMS.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. A connection to AWS KMS can be made through a private endpoint in a VPC instead of connecting over the internet. When you use a VPC endpoint, communication between your VPC and AWS KMS is conducted entirely within the AWS network./ppA VPC interface endpoint connects a VPC directly to AWS KMS without an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN connection, or AWS Direct Connect connection. The instances in a VPC do not need public IP addresses to communicate with AWS KMS./ppFor more information about connecting to AWS KMS through a VPC endpoint, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/kms-vpc-endpoint.html"Connecting to AWS KMS through a VPC endpoint/a.

question_content: pA company is creating an application that will keep records. The application will run on Amazon EC2 instances and will use an Amazon Aurora MySQL database as its data store. To maintain compliance, the application must not retain information that is determined to be sensitive./p  pWhich technique should a SysOps administrator use to detect if sensitive data is being stored in the application?

answer_choices.choice_content: pExport data from the database by using an AWS Lambda function. Store the data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Macie to examine the stored data. Examine the report for any sensitive data that is discovered.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The important requirement in this question is the need to examine properly authorized data for content that might not be advisable for compliance reasons. An application might include a free notes field where users might inadvertently store their credit card information. Macie is designed to look through Amazon S3 to discover this kind of sensitive information and flag the findings for remediation./ppIn this scenario, the data is stored in an Aurora database. To take advantage of the machine learning engine that Macie uses, we must first extract the data from the database and store it in Amazon S3. Lambda becomes the easiest solution because it avoids changing the core application that runs on EC2 instances. Lambda also is scalable for the future./ppFor more information about Macie, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/what-is-macie.html"What is Amazon Macie?/a /ppFor more information about how to use managed data identifiers in Macie, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/managed-data-identifiers.html"Using managed data identifiers in Amazon Macie/a. /ppFor more information about how to integrate Lambda with Aurora, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraMySQL.Integrating.Lambda.html"Invoking a Lambda function from an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster/a. /ppFor more information about a similar scenario that shows how to use Macie on data that is extracted from data sources (DynamoDB in this case), see a   href="https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/detecting-sensitive-data-in-dynamodb-with-macie/"Detecting sensitive data in DynamoDB with Macie/a. /pp

answer_choices.choice_content: pInstall the Amazon GuardDuty plugin for Aurora. Configure GuardDuty to examine the database. Add the corresponding EC2 CIDR ranges to the trusted IP list in GuardDuty. Examine the report for any sensitive data that is discovered.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. GuardDuty is a threat detection service that continuously monitors for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior to protect AWS accounts, workloads, and data that is stored in Amazon S3. While GuardDuty looks for security breaches, GuardDuty is not installable as a plugin for Aurora. Also, GuardDuty does not classify data that is saved.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDeploy Amazon Inspector by installing the Amazon Inspector agent on all EC2 instances. Set the Amazon Inspector assessment type to HOST assessment. Include NETWORK communications with the Aurora DB cluster. Examine the report for any sensitive data that is discovered.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon Inspector is an automated security assessment service that helps improve the security and compliance of applications that are deployed on AWS. Amazon Inspector automatically assesses applications for exposure, vulnerabilities, and deviations from best practices. However, Amazon Inspector will not flag any data that is being properly transferred between an authorized application and an authorized database, even if that data would be classified as sensitive. Also, the Network Assessment option in Amazon Inspector examines all network connections and is not used to specifically track one connection.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse VPC Flow Logs to examine traffic between the EC2 instances and the Aurora DB cluster. Store the log files in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Detective to examine the extracted log files. Examine the report for any sensitive data that is discovered.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Detective helps analyze, investigate, and quickly identify the root cause of potential security issues or suspicious activities. Detective automatically collects log data from AWS resources and uses machine learning, statistical analysis, and graph theory to build a linked set of data for faster and more efficient security investigations. While Detective will examine VPC Flow Logs for suspicious traffic, there is nothing suspicious about the communications between the application and the database. The flow logs would not contain the actual transaction, so there would be no data about the contents of the communication for Detective to examine.

question_content: pOn a weekly basis, the administrator for a photo sharing website receives an archive of all files that users have uploaded the previous week. These file archives can be as large as 10 TB in size. For legal reasons, these archives must be saved in such a way that no one can delete or modify them. Occasionally, there might be a need to view the contents, but retrieval can take 3 or more hours./p  pWhat should the administrator do with the weekly archive to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpload the file to Amazon S3 through the AWS Management Console. Apply an S3 Lifecycle policy to change the storage class to S3 Glacier.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The file size in this scenario can be greater than 5 TB, so a direct upload to Amazon S3 is not an option.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpload the archive to Amazon S3 Glacier with the AWS CLI. Use S3 Glacier Vault Lock.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. S3 Glacier supports archives that are larger than 5 TB. It also offers S3 Glacier Vault Lock, a feature that can prevent the deletion or modification of the archives./ppFor more information about how to upload an archive in S3 Glacier, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonglacier/latest/dev/uploading-an-archive.html"Uploading an Archive in Amazon S3 Glacier/a. /ppFor more information about S3 Glacier Vault Lock, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonglacier/latest/dev/vault-lock.html"Amazon S3 Glacier Vault Lock/a. /pp

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a Linux Amazon EC2 instance with an encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Copy each weekly archive file to this instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The use of Amazon EC2 and Amazon EBS can work, but this solution does not address the legal requirement to prevent deletion or modification. This solution also is significantly more expensive and more complex than the correct answer.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a file gateway that is attached to a file share on an S3 bucket with the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Upload the archives through the gateway.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The file size in this scenario can be greater than 5 TB, and a file gateway does not support that size.

question_content: pA SysOps administrator wants to encrypt an existing Amazon RDS DB instance with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)./p  pHow should the SysOps administrator accomplish this goal?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCopy the data volumes of the unencrypted instance. Apply the KMS key to the copied data volumes. Start the instance with the encrypted volumes.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The data volumes in Amazon RDS are unlike data volumes in Amazon EC2. The data volumes in Amazon RDS cannot be accessed or encrypted separately. Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service, and you do not have access to the underlying resources./ppFor more information about RDS DB instance storage, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_Storage.html"Amazon RDS DB instance storage/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a read replica of the unencrypted instance. Encrypt the read replica with the KMS key. Promote the read replica to become the primary instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot have an encrypted read replica of an unencrypted DB instance, and you cannot have an unencrypted read replica of an encrypted DB instance. Additionally, encrypted read replicas must be encrypted with the same key as the source DB instance when both are in the same AWS Region./ppFor more information about limitations of RDS encryption, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.html#Overview.Encryption.Limitations"Limitations of Amazon RDS encrypted DB instances/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pTake a snapshot of the unencrypted instance. Apply the KMS key to the existing instance using the modify-db-instance command. Restart the instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can enable encryption for an RDS DB instance only when you create the DB instance, not after you create the DB instance. However, you can create a snapshot of your DB instance, create an encrypted copy of that snapshot, and restore a new DB instance from the encrypted snapshot./ppFor more information about RDS encryption, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.html"Encrypting Amazon RDS resources/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pTake a snapshot of the unencrypted instance. Create an encrypted copy of the snapshot with the KMS key. Restore the instance from the encrypted snapshot.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can create a snapshot of your DB instance, create an encrypted copy of that snapshot, and restore a new DB instance from the encrypted snapshot./ppFor more information about RDS encryption, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.html"Encrypting Amazon RDS resources/a.

question_content: pA company is required to encrypt data at rest for all of its Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes in the us-east-1 Region./ppWhich operationally efficient solution will ensure that encryption is enabled for all new EBS volumes?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution will notify the company when unencrypted EBS volumes are created. It will not prevent the creation of unencrypted volumes.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the encrypted-volumes AWS Config managed rule.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution will identify unencrypted EBS volumes in all Regions. It will not prevent the creation of unencrypted volumes.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an IAM policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution will work, but it is not operationally efficient. It requires much more management at the policy level and the user level. It also increases the risk that users will create unencrypted volumes.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet the default encryption status in the settings of the Amazon EC2 console.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. A solution that requires encryption by default for the Region is the most operationally efficient way to ensure that new volumes are created using encryption./ppFor more information about encryption requirements, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/EBSEncryption.html#encryption-by-default"Encryption by default/a.

question_content: pA company has a VPC that has a private IP address space of 10.0.0.0/16. The company has used up all the existing private IP space. A SysOps administrator must resolve this issue with a solution that minimizes complexity and maximizes cost-effectiveness./ppWhich solution meets these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConvert the IP addresses to IPv6 to create many more available addresses.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. All Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC are dual stacked, having both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. It is not possible to assign more IPv6 addresses than the number of IPv4 addresses that are available.

answer_choices.choice_content: pChange the private IP address space from 10.0.0.0/16 to 10.0.0.0/8.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The largest IP block available in a VPC is a /16.

answer_choices.choice_content: pFind an unused block of private IP addresses. Add that block to the VPC.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The solution is to add more CIDR ranges. The solution takes fewer steps than setting up a new VPC and establishing VPC peering. This can be less expensive because there is no charge for data that is transferred between EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone if private IP addresses are used./ppFor more information about how to add CIDR blocks to an existing VPC, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/how-it-works.html" How Amazon VPC works/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up a new VPC with a new private address space. Establish VPC peering between the two VPCs.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The creation of another VPC will increase cost and complexity. Charges are incurred for data that is transferred from one VPC to another, even if the VPCs are in the same AWS Region. Complexity is increased because a second VPC is needed and because the route tables on both VPCs must be modified.

question_content: pA company has a web application that is deployed in a VPC. Inbound traffic to this web application comes in through an internet gateway and arrives at a Network Load Balancer (NLB). From there, the traffic travels to multiple Amazon EC2 instances in two private subnets. The company wants to perform deep packet inspection on the inbound traffic to identify potential hacking attempts./ppWhich solution meets these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure AWS Shield for the VPC.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Shield provides protection against DDoS attacks. Shield does not perform deep packet inspection./ppFor more information about Shield, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/shield-chapter.html"AWS Shield/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Network Firewall on the VPC. Configure Network Firewall to perform deep packet inspection.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Network Firewall can be configured to be stateful or stateless. Also, Network Firewall can be configured to perform deep packet inspection./ppFor more information about Network Firewall, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-network-firewall.html" What is AWS Network Firewall?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Network Firewall on the subnets. Configure Network Firewall to perform deep packet inspection.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Network Firewall does not work on the subnet level. Network Firewall works on the VPC level./ppFor more information about Network Firewall, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-network-firewall.html"What is AWS Network Firewall?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up Traffic Mirroring on an inbound port of the NLB.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Traffic Mirroring copies inbound and outbound traffic from the elastic network interfaces that are attached to EC2 instances. However, to gather insights on this traffic, you would need to take an additional step to send the mirrored traffic to the network interface of another EC2 instance, or to an NLB that has a UDP listener./ppFor more information about Traffic Mirroring, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/what-is-traffic-mirroring.html" What is Traffic Mirroring?/a/ppFor more information about Traffic Mirroring, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-how-it-works.html" How Traffic Mirroring works/a.

question_content: pA company needs to deploy a web application on two Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Two EC2 instances will also be deployed to host the database. The infrastructure needs to be designed across Availability Zones (AZs) for high availability and must limit public access to the instances as much as possible./ppHow should this be achieved within a VPC?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse two AZs and create a public subnet in each AZ for the Application Load Balancer, a private subnet in each AZ for the web servers, and a private subnet in each AZ for the database servers.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The ALB is in a public subnet and can forward the traffic to a private subnet. The use of private subnets where possible follows the Well-Architected Framework approach. The creation of subnets in each Availability Zone gives the application high availability./ppFor more information about VPCs, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/how-it-works.html" How Amazon VPC works/a./ppFor more information about the Well-Architected Framework as it applies to public access to resources, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/permissions-management.html" Permissions Management/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse two AZs and create a public subnet in each AZ for the Application Load Balancer, a public subnet in each AZ for the web servers, and a public subnet in each AZ for the database servers.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. There is no need to put the web servers in a public subnet because the ALB is in a public subnet. To adhere to the Well Architected Framework, you should limit exposure of your resources to public subnets./ppFor more information about the Well-Architected Framework as it applies to public access to resources, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/permissions-management.html"Permissions Management/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse two AZs and create one public subnet for the Application Load Balancer, a private subnet in each AZ for the web servers, and a public subnet in each AZ for the database servers.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Subnets cannot extend across Availability Zones. Therefore, the ALB cannot exist in a single subnet and also in two Availability Zones./ppFor more information about VPCs, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/how-it-works.html" How Amazon VPC works/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse two AZs and create one public subnet for the Application Load Balancer, a public subnet in each AZ for the web servers, and a private subnet in each AZ for the database servers.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Subnets cannot extend across Availability Zones. Therefore, the ALB cannot exist in a single subnet and also in two Availability Zones. Additionally, there is no need to put the web servers in a public subnet because the ALB is in a public subnet. To adhere to the Well Architected Framework, you should limit exposure of your resources to public subnets./ppFor more information about VPCs, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/how-it-works.html" How Amazon VPC works/a./ppFor more information about the Well-Architected Framework as it applies to public access to resources, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/permissions-management.html" Permissions Management/a.

question_content: pA SysOps administrator needs to perform deep packet inspection on a particular traffic flow. The traffic flow goes from one VPC to a separate VPC within the same AWS Region./ppWhich solution meets these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up VPC Flow Logs on the destination VPC. Configure filters to look for this specific traffic. Send these flow logs to Amazon CloudWatch with alarming turned on.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. VPC Flow Logs do not perform deep packet inspection.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up VPC Flow Logs on the source instances. Configure VPC Flow Log filters to look for this specific traffic. Send these flow logs to Amazon CloudWatch with alarming turned on.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. VPC Flow Logs do not perform deep packet inspection.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up Traffic Mirroring on the destination VPC. Configure filters to look for this specific traffic. Send the captured traffic to a target instance that is set up in the destination VPC.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. While Traffic Mirroring allows for deep packet inspection, Traffic Mirroring must be set up on the elastic network interface, not the VPC.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up Traffic Mirroring on the originating instances. Configure filters to look for this specific traffic. Send the captured traffic to a target instance that is set up in the destination VPC.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Traffic Mirroring copies inbound and outbound traffic from the network interfaces that are attached to Amazon EC2 instances. You can send the mirrored traffic to the network interface of another EC2 instance, or to a Network Load Balancer that has a UDP listener. Filters can reduce the traffic that gets mirrored./ppFor more information about traffic mirror source and target connectivity options, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-connection.html" Traffic mirror source and target connectivity options/a.

question_content: pA company is building a web service on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. External clients must be able to add specific public IP addresses to an allow list in their firewalls to access the company's web service./ppWhich load balancer or ELB feature should the company use to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pApplication Load Balancer
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Application Load Balancers can balance traffic between clients and a web service. However, Application Load Balancers cannot have a specific (static) public IP address, which is required for the client's firewall allow list./ppFor more information about Application Load Balancers, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/introduction.html"What is an Application Load Balancer?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pGateway Load Balancer
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Gateway Load Balancers can balance traffic between third-party virtual network appliances to inspect incoming and outbound traffic flows. The scenario requires a solution to balance traffic to a web service./ppFor more information  about Gateway Load Balancers, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/introduction.html"What is a Gateway Load Balancer?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pNetwork Load Balancer
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. In the scenario, external clients need specific (static) public IP addresses to add to their firewall allow list for outbound traffic. You can associate Elastic IP addresses with internet-facing Network Load Balancers./ppFor more information about Network Load Balancers, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/introduction.html" What is a Network Load Balancer?/a/ppFor more information about Elastic IP addresses, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-eips.html" Elastic IP addresses/a./ppFor more information about how to associate Elastic IP addresses with a Network Load Balancer, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/create-network-load-balancer.html#configure-load-balancer" Configure a load balancer and a listener/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pLoad balancer target groups
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Load balancers are associated with target groups. Target groups route requests to one or more registered targets or instances. A target group alone would not provide the required resources to route traffic from external clients to the web service./ppFor more information  about target groups, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-target-groups.html"Target groups for your Network Load Balancers/a.

question_content: pAn Amazon EC2 instance is running in a private subnet. A SysOps administrator is able to use SSH to connect to the EC2 instance from a bastion host instance that runs inside the same VPC subnet./ppWhen the SysOps administrator attempts to ping the EC2 instance from the bastion host instance, no response is received. ICMP traffic must be allowed, according to company policy./ppWhat should the SysOps administrator do to troubleshoot this issue?

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the inbound rules of the security group that is associated with the target instance by adding an All ICMP - IPv4 Allow rule. Include the private subnet's CIDR range as the source IP address.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The ping command is a type of ICMP traffic. Security groups block all inbound traffic by default. Even if the security group allows SSH traffic between instances or other types of TCP traffic, ICMP must be explicitly added to the security group./ppTo ping an instance over IPv4, you must add the following inbound ICMP rule to a security group that is assigned to the instance:/ppProtocol type: ICMPbrProtocol number: 1brICMP type: 8 (echo)brICMP code: N/A/ppSource IP address: The public IPv4 address of your computer, or a range of IPv4 addresses (in CIDR block notation) in your local network./ppThe settings are similar for IPv6./ppFor more information about setting up the ping command in a security group, see a  href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/security-group-rules-reference.html#sg-rules-ping" Rules for ping/ICMP/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the inbound rules of the network ACL that is associated with the private subnet by adding an All ICMP - IPv4 Allow rule. Include the private subnet's CIDR range as the source IP address.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Because the bastion host instance and the EC2 instance are in the same subnet, network ACL rules will not be evaluated. There is no need to add ICMP to the network ACL rules./ppFor more information about network ACLs, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html"Network ACLs/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the route table that is associated with the private subnet by adding an All ICMP - IPv4 Allow rule. Include the private subnet's CIDR range as the source IP address.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The route tables direct traffic based on IP address, not protocol. Because the bastion host instance can use SSH to connect to the EC2 instance, the route table is already directing traffic freely between the two instances and is not causing the problem./ppFor more information about route tables, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Route_Tables.html"Route tables for your VPC/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the rules of the virtual private gateway that is associated with the VPC by adding an All ICMP - IPv4 Allow rule. Include the private subnet's CIDR range as the source IP address.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Virtual private gateways do not have rule sets. There is nothing that can be edited to allow or deny specific protocols at the virtual private gateway level./ppFore more information about virtual private gateways, see a   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/virtualgateways.html"Virtual private gateway associations/a.

question_content: pA company is ready to test a new version of its application. The company needs to send a small number of visitors to the new version to verify that the application is performing correctly./p  pWhich Amazon Route 53 routing policy can the company use to meet this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: pSimple routing policy
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A simple routing policy is used to route traffic to a single resource, such as a web server for a website.

answer_choices.choice_content: pGeolocation routing policy
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A geolocation routing policy is used to route traffic based on the location of the application users.

answer_choices.choice_content: pMultivalue answer routing policy

answer_choices.choice_content: pWeighted routing policy
